title: Predator

compareCandidate.label: Predator vs. prey
compareCandidate.description: A predator hunts and eats other animals. Prey is the animal being hunted and eaten. The same species can be both - a fox is a predator to a rabbit but prey to a wolf.

plainLanguageExplanation: A predator is an animal that hunts and eats other animals. Predators come in many forms - a lion, an eagle, a wolf, or a dragonfly all hunt for their food. To be good hunters, predators are often equipped with speed, sharp senses, sharp teeth or claws, and good camouflage. Predators matter to an ecosystem because they keep prey populations in check - without predators, prey numbers can grow too high and damage their own food supply. Predators and prey exist in a constant race of better hunting against better escaping.

keyFacts.label: Balance
keyFacts.value: Predator and prey are in a constant race of hunt vs. escape

whyItMatters: Predators shape the whole ecosystem - by keeping prey numbers in check, they stop one species from using up all the resources. Understanding them explains why top hunters matter far beyond the animals they eat.
didYouKnow: A cheetah can accelerate from 0 to 100 km/h in about three seconds - faster than most sports cars - all to catch its prey.
